title: From agent work to a readable browser presentation
summary: Use one-pager when you want to understand the agent’s output in a browser. Choose the presentation style, then read one coherent document with useful visuals and expandable detail.

blocks.text: A one-pager is a single HTML document, not necessarily a single printed page. The overview stays concise; deeper evidence and mechanics can expand when you need them.

blocks.title: Presentation workflow
blocks.description: A presentation preference shapes the document. It does not approve the underlying proposal or authorize implementation.

items.title: Ask for a presentation
items.text: Invoke /skill:one-pager with the topic, or ask the agent to make a one-pager from the material already discussed.

items.title: Choose the style
items.text: If unspecified, pick one of the four modes or Combine modes. A combination requires at least two selections. Explicitly naming modes skips the questions.

items.title: Read in the browser
items.text: The agent creates and opens the HTML. Use the contents navigation and expand supporting detail when needed.

blocks.title: What stays local, and what needs explicit submission?

blocks.text: The page has no background network requests. External source links open only when followed. Decision-review positions are draft feedback: export and submit them through the project’s real acceptance process. The page never changes an ADR or authorizes implementation.
